text: Writing clean code is an important skill for every programmer. Clean code is easy to read and understand, even for people who did not write it. One key habit is following naming conventions. Use clear, meaningful names for variables and functions, so others can quickly see what they do. Another good practice is keeping functions small and focused on one task. This makes your code simpler to test and fix. Clean code is also easier to maintain over time. When you or your teammates need to update the program later, well-organized code saves hours of work and prevents mistakes.
